data.why: The repo bundles its own complete example data under 'data set/' (Table A, Table B, training_data.csv, supertable.csv, predictions.csv) and website/data/predictions.csv plus precomputed figure images in website/data/Images/; Virtual_Lab.py and Report.py read these directly, so nothing needs to be copied or synthesized.

goals: Select a bacterium and antibiotic and compare the ML model's predicted resistance rate against the real ATLAS-observed rate, when available
Compare the formula-based (V1) resistance score against the gradient-boosting model's (V2) prediction for the same pair
Inspect which resistance mechanisms (efflux pump, hydrolysis, porin loss, etc.) contribute most to a given pair's resistance via the pie chart breakdown
Identify bacteria-antibiotic pairs with no ATLAS ground truth, where the model's prediction is an extrapolation
Read the full project report to understand model validation (leave-one-out cross-validation, MAE, R²) and known limitations

review.summary: The tree gets the app's purpose right (V1 vs V2 vs ATLAS for a chosen pair, mechanism breakdown, validation and limits), and every screen I opened matches its node. Before filing it needs: the donut labelled as a breakdown of V1 formula weights, the bacteria count fixed, and tasks added for screening across drugs and for checking that bacteria with identical profiles get identical predictions.
